title: Portable Driver Triage — rejected.jsonl row
description: One JSON document per line in reports/rejected.jsonl. Represents a binary that failed the L0 viability gate and therefore never got a reports/<sha256>/ directory. Append-only, never mutated. If the same binary is re-presented and rejected again (e.g., pipeline upgrade changed L0 heuristics), a new row is appended.

schema_version.description: Row schema version. Pipeline upgrades bump this; readers may skip or down-convert older rows during a migration window.

sha256.description: SHA256 of the binary that was rejected. Always computable — rejection never happens before hashing.

driver_file.description: Original filename as extracted from the parent installer. Null when the extraction step itself could not resolve a name.

source_path.description: Where this binary came from, relative to the project root or an absolute scratchpad path. Lets a researcher re-visit the parent installer when triaging rejections.

size_bytes.description: Null only when the file was unreadable or truncated to zero on arrival.

arch.description: Architecture if detectable. Null when the PE header itself could not be parsed.

reason.description: Closed vocabulary. Meanings: not-pe = file is not a PE at all; wrong-subsystem = PE but IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM is not NATIVE; kernel-imports-unresolved = PE+NATIVE but imports do not resolve against kernel modules (ntoskrnl.exe, hal.dll, wdfldr.sys, …); signature-policy-mismatch = failed the signature filter chosen for this run (see run.flags.signature in the paired index_row); corrupted = structural corruption or truncation; packed-unknown = packed with a packer the pipeline cannot unpack; blacklisted = operator explicitly opted this hash out.

reason_detail.description: Human-readable specifics. For wrong-subsystem, state the actual subsystem value. For kernel-imports-unresolved, name the first unresolved import. For packed-unknown, name the detected packer or 'entropy heuristic'.

detected_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, must end with Z.
